2022_29_policy_changes_recommendation_ot.paragraph: Three bundled memoranda supporting a Troy School District Board of Education policy discussion: a September 15, 2022 memo from Rick West of the Business Office laying out Policy Manual updates recommended by Miller Johnson School Policy Services, the Board Policy Committee, and District Administration; a September 19, 2022 Miller Johnson memo replacing the Open Meetings Act remote-participation language in Policy 1002; and a September 1, 2022 Michigan Department of Education memo on Section 98c learning loss funding. Most consequential is Section 98c of Public Act 144 of 2022 (MCL 388.1698c), appropriating $52,056,000 in federal GEER/ESSER II money, with district applications due November 30, 2022.
2022_29_policy_changes_recommendation_ot.page:
**Source and authorship**
Memorandum to the Board of Education from Rick West, dated September 15, 2022, subject "Policy Manual Recommended Updates," issued from the Business Office at 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098 (phone 248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013). Revisions were recommended jointly by Miller Johnson School Policy Services, the Board of Education Policy Committee, and District Administration, and are organized by Policy Manual series.

**Introduction and Bylaws (0000 and 1000 series)**
Policy 0000.03 (The Superintendent of Schools) gains two additions: express authority for the Superintendent to make employment decisions, including hiring and termination, for all non-administrative and non-teaching staff; and authority for the Superintendent to select the School District bargaining team, with the Board approving all team members prior to the start of negotiations and ratifying all negotiated agreements. Administrative Regulations are not effective for one month from the date provided to the Board. Policy 1000.01 renames the sub-policy "Removal from Office" to "Removal from Officer Positions."

**Students (2000 series)**
Policy 2000.01, "Children of Non-Resident Employees," is rewritten to close a loophole allowing a pupil to remain enrolled tuition-free after the parent voluntarily leaves employment; continued attendance is preserved only while the employee remains employed, or where the employee's departure was due to layoff or elimination of the position. "Employee" is defined as an individual with regularly scheduled hours while school is in session, excluding seasonal, coaching, and third-party contracted employees, including substitute teachers. Policy 2000.06 adds personal electronic device rules: use permitted only before and after the regular school day, during the student's scheduled lunch, or as directed by staff for educational purposes; devices otherwise powered off and out of sight; no recording or broadcasting of any student, staff member, or other person without permission, excepting athletic events, arts performances, and similar activities. Policy 2000.07 and 2000.07-AR update Wellness language.

**Curriculum and Instruction (3000 series)**
The entire 3000 section was reviewed given escalating attacks on schools over curriculum. Policy 3000.01 ties curriculum to legally-compliant, research-based standards and states that core academic curriculum changes require Board approval to the extent required by MCL 380.1278. Policy 3000.02 is renamed "Parent and Family Engagement (PFE)" and aligned to Title I. Policy 3000.03 drops an extraneous word. Policy 3000.04 is fully replaced as "Textbooks, Technology, and Other Essential Curricular Materials," citing MCL 380.1421/22 and delegating approval and purchase of non-textbook instructional materials to the Superintendent. Policy 3000.05 is retitled "Selection of Media Center/Library Materials."

**Personnel, Business, General (4000, 5000, 8000 series)**
Policy 4000.03 adds authority to require a medical examination on reasonable suspicion of drug, alcohol, or illegal substance influence, with all costs borne by the School District and reports kept in a separate confidential personnel file. Policy 5000.03 gains a new "Real Property and Structures" acquisition sub-policy; Policy 5000.05's disposition sub-policy is renamed to match. Policy 5000.11 deletes the list of fundraising sites (DonorsChoose.org, Kickstarter.com, GoFundMe.com, CrowdRise.com). No 6000 series changes. Policy 8000.07 is revised for Title IX and designates the Assistant Superintendent of Employees Services and Title IX Coordinator.

**Attached memoranda**
A September 19, 2022 Miller Johnson memo offers Option A and Option B replacements for the Open Meetings Act remote-participation language in Policy 1002. A September 1, 2022 MDE memo from Deputy Superintendent Delsa D. Chapman covers Section 98c learning loss funds of $52,056,000.
2022_29_policy_changes_recommendation_ot.verbose:
**Cover memorandum.** Rick West wrote to the Troy School District Board of Education on September 15, 2022, subject "Policy Manual Recommended Updates," on Business Office letterhead showing 4400 Livernois, Troy, MI 48098, phone 248.823.4022, fax 248.823.4013. The updates were recommended by Miller Johnson School Policy Services, the Board of Education Policy Committee, and District Administration, and are organized by Policy Manual section.

**Introduction - 0000 Series.** Policy 0000.03, The Superintendent of Schools, gains two additions. The Superintendent, employed in conformity with the Revised School Code as chief administrator, is authorized by the Board to make employment decisions, including hiring and termination, for all non-administrative and non-teaching staff, and develops Administrative Regulations that, except as otherwise agreed by the Board, will not be effective for a period of one month from the date provided to the Board; the Board may but need not formally approve them, and references to the Superintendent include his/her designee. On collective bargaining, the Board is represented in all labor negotiation proceedings by a negotiating team whose members the Board approves prior to the start of negotiations, the Superintendent shall select the bargaining team, and all negotiated agreements are subject to Board ratification.

**Bylaws - 1000 Series.** Policy 1000.01, Organization and Functioning of the Board, renames the sub-policy "Removal from Office" to "Removal from Officer Positions," since it concerns removal of Board officers from officer positions rather than removal from the Board itself.

**Students - 2000 Series.** Policy 2000.01, Admission and Enrollment, sub-policy "Children of Non-Resident Employees," is rewritten consistent with the State Aid Act and the Pupil Accounting Manual to close a loophole under which a person could obtain employment, enroll a child, then voluntarily leave employment while the pupil kept tuition-free enrollment. A child of a non-resident employee may enroll without tuition in the K-12 program and continue through graduation or a certificate of completion while the employee remains employed, or if the employee's departure was due to layoff or elimination of the position; long-term suspension or expulsion under the Student Code of Conduct is not barred. "Employee" means an individual with regularly scheduled hours while school is in session, excluding seasonal, coaching, and third-party contracted employees including substitute teachers, with eligibility starting at the next school term/semester.

Policy 2000.06, Behavior, defines a personal electronic device as a privately owned device used for audio, video, or text communications. Use is permitted only before and after the regular school day, during the student's scheduled lunch time, and as directed by a teacher or other professional staff member for educational purposes; otherwise devices must be powered off and out of sight in backpacks/purses or lockers. Students may not broadcast or record audio, images, or video of any student, staff member, or other person in school or at a school-related activity without permission, except for activities where personal recording is generally permitted such as athletic events and arts performances. Policy 2000.07, Health and Safety, updates Wellness in both policy and administrative regulation 2000.07-AR for compliance with the latest federal regulatory guidance on student wellness and nutrition.

**Curriculum and Instruction - 3000 Series.** Citing the current political environment and escalating attacks on schools and boards over curriculum development and approval, the whole 3000 section was reviewed. Policy 3000.01, Curriculum Development, directs the Superintendent to develop, implement, and evaluate the core academic curriculum, consistent with the Board's policy on Student Learning and Achievement, meeting or exceeding all State of Michigan requirements, standards based on legally-compliant, research-based grade level learning and achievement standards leading to a School District diploma, and addressing career and technical education, students of all abilities and with disabilities, and gifted students; core curriculum changes require Board approval to the extent required by MCL 380.1278. Policy 3000.02 is renamed "Parent and Family Engagement (PFE)," with regulations covering skill development, review of curriculum, textbooks, and teaching materials, observation of instruction other than testing and assessments, and disclosure of student information for sales or marketing, plus Title I duties to inform and train parents and staff, consult regularly, involve families in program design and evaluation, and enable participation by those lacking literacy skills or whose native language is not English, with services in Title I schools comparable to non-Title I schools. Policy 3000.03, Instruction (cited in the memo body as 3003.03), drops an extraneous word, leaving instruction delivered to the maximum extent feasible using research based and peer reviewed instructional methodologies. Policy 3000.04 is comprehensively replaced and retitled "Textbooks, Technology, and Other Essential Curricular Materials" from "Textbooks and Other Instructional Materials"; textbooks are recommended to the Board for approval to the extent required by MCL 380.1421/22, while the Board delegates to the Superintendent authority to approve and purchase other instructional materials, which need no Board approval but must be compatible with the approved core curriculum. Policy 3000.05 is retitled "Selection of Media Center/Library Materials," authorizing the Superintendent to approve purchases for the media center and classroom libraries on recommendations from professional staff members, parents, and students.

**Personnel - 4000 Series.** Policy 4000.03, Conditions of Employment, sub-policy Alcohol and Drug Free Workplace, lets the Superintendent require a medical examination on reasonable suspicion that an employee is under the influence of drugs, alcohol, or illegal substances while performing job duties or on school grounds; employees or volunteers who unlawfully manufacture, distribute, dispense, possess, or use alcohol or any drug in the workplace, or are present under the influence, face discipline up to and including discharge. The Medical Examinations sub-policy lists triggers: required or permitted by federal or state law; required or permitted by the employment contract; information suggesting a health condition may negatively affect performance of essential functions with or without accommodations; information suggesting a direct threat to the employee's safety or that of others; insufficient medical documentation for a health leave after a chance to supplement; and reasonable suspicion of influence. All costs are borne by the School District, the employee signs a release for the physician to report directly to the Superintendent, and the report is kept in a separate confidential personnel file.

**Business - 5000 Series.** A new sub-policy "Real Property and Structures" is added to Policy 5000.03, Purchasing, because baseline policies covered only disposition of land, buildings, facilities, and real estate without matching acquisition authority, and because title agencies routinely require a board resolution and a document authorizing an individual, most commonly the Board President or Superintendent, to execute closing documents; Board approval is required for both the process and the purchase, and the Superintendent may execute all closing documents. Under Policy 5000.05, Surplus Property, the sub-policy "Land, Buildings, Facilities, and Real Estate" is renamed "Real Property and Structures" for sale or disposition, with parallel provisions; the memo notes the two share a title but differ in objective and impact. Policy 5000.11, Online Fundraising, deletes the list of services DonorsChoose.org, Kickstarter.com, GoFundMe.com, and CrowdRise.com; no employee may create, post, or sponsor an online fundraiser without prior written consent from the Superintendent, and property secured becomes District property.

**Facilities and Operations - 6000 Series:** no recommended updates. **School and Community Relations - 7000 Series** is listed without changes.

**General Policies - 8000 Series.** Policy 8000.07, Discrimination and Harassment, and regulation 8000.07-AR are revised for Title IX. The U.S. Department of Education issued new guidelines in 2020, updating the regulations for the first time since 1997, and the 2021-22 school year was the first meaningful opportunity for most districts to live with them in a normal school year. Draft Title IX regulations issued in June 2022 are not final and are not integrated; finalization is not expected until approximately late 2023. The policy bars discrimination or harassment based on race, color, national origin, religion, sex (including sexual orientation and gender identity), marital status, genetic information, disability, age, or any other basis prohibited by law, and designates the Assistant Superintendent of Employees Services and Title IX Coordinator to supervise implementation.

**Miller Johnson Open Meetings Act memo.** Dated September 19, 2022, from MJ School Policy Services to MJ Policy Service Clients, concerning Policy 1002 ("Meetings of the Board of Education"). The July 2022 Electronic Meetings and Remote Participation language is marked OUTDATED AS OF 9/16/22 UPDATE. Both replacement options permit remote participation only for absence due to military leave or reasonable accommodation for a disability; medical condition and local state of emergency/disaster bases were removed because the Open Meetings Act no longer permits them. Attorney General Nessel released an opinion letter earlier in the year holding a board member with a disability must be accommodated, reasoning the Americans with Disabilities Act negates the OMA where compliance would require violating the ADA. The memo weighs MCL 15.263a(1), allowing electronic meetings, against MCL 15.263a(8), limiting electronic participation to members absent on military duty, and argues members may still contribute remotely if not counted toward a quorum and not a deciding vote. Option A requires physical presence to participate except as otherwise permitted by the OMA; Option B requires physical presence only to be counted toward a quorum or to vote. Conditions for military-duty or disability remote attendance: advance notice consistent with MCL 15.263a(4) and agenda posting consistent with MCL 15.263a(5); the Board Secretary recording each remote member's name in the minutes plus an opening announcement that, except for military duty, identifies the member's location by state and city, township, county, or village; 2-way communication; notice to the Board President at least one business day before the meeting; and steps such as roll call voting. Questions go to Policy@MillerJohnson.com.

**Michigan Department of Education Section 98c memo.** Dated September 1, 2022, to Local and Intermediate School District Superintendents and Public School Academy Directors, from Delsa D. Chapman, Ed.D., Deputy Superintendent, Division of Educator, Student, and School Supports, subject "Public Act 144 of 2022 - Section 98c - Learning Loss." MDE opened the application window September 15, 2022 for LEAs, both traditional districts and public school academies. PA 144 of 2022 (MCL 388.1698c) was signed July 14, 2022 by Governor Gretchen Whitmer and appropriates $52,056,000 in federal funding under the Governor's Emergency Education Relief (GEER) Fund and the federal Elementary and Secondary School Emergency Relief (ESSER) II Fund. Applications were due no later than November 30, 2022 and required an assurance that by not later than October 30, 2022 a presentation on use of the funds would be given at a public meeting of the LEA board, a link to the learning loss plan posted on the LEA website with an assurance to post updates, and a brief description of district metrics. Recipients must report to MDE by July 14, 2023 on funds spent, services provided, students reached, metrics, and impact, feeding a single legislative report due August 15, 2023; funds are recaptured if a district misses the deadline. ESSER II targets low-income students, children with disabilities, English learners, racial and ethnic minorities, students experiencing homelessness, and children and youth in foster care via reliable assessments, evidence-based activities, parent and family assistance, and tracking of engagement in distance learning. Funding is distributed to each LEA in an equal amount per pupil in membership, calculated after the November 30 close, with disbursement anticipated in the early winter state school aid payments. The application link is https://mdoe.state.mi.us/gems/public/QuestionnaireHome.aspx?code=i4d1tcbt; technical assistance meetings were set for 2:30 p.m. EST on September 19, 2022 and 11:00 a.m. EST on November 4, 2022; application questions go to mde-gems@michigan.gov and learning loss questions to Ruth Anne Hodges at hodgesr3@michigan.gov, with copies to the Michigan Education Alliance and the Confederation of Michigan Tribal Education Departments. The letterhead lists State Board of Education members Casandra E. Ulbrich (President), Pamela Pugh (Vice President), Tiffany D. Tilley (Secretary), Tom McMillin (Treasurer), Judith Pritchett (NASBE Delegate), Ellen Cogen Lipton, and Nikki Snyder, State Superintendent Michael F. Rice, Ph.D., Governor Gretchen Whitmer, and 608 West Allegan Street, P.O. Box 30008, Lansing, Michigan 48909, telephone 833-633-5788.

**Overall observations.** Because Michigan state aid payments had not yet been posted to the General Fund as of September 30, the General Fund actual revenue column reflects essentially only local property tax collections and interdistrict receipts, while expenditures had begun in full with the start of the school year, producing the reported shortfall. 2022_31_2_d_bond_resolution_sbqlp_troy_2.paragraph: A resolution of the Troy School District Board of Education, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, authorizing 2023 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation), presented for adoption at a regular meeting on December 13, 2022. It authorizes the first series under the $555,000,000 bond proposal approved by district voters at the General School Election on November 8, 2022, in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $190,000,000, with true interest cost capped at 6.50% per annum and final maturity no later than thirty years from the date of issue. Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated is appointed senior managing underwriter for a negotiated sale.
2022_31_2_d_bond_resolution_sbqlp_troy_2.page:
**Instrument and setting**
Resolution Authorizing 2023 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation), Troy School District, County of Oakland, State of Michigan, drafted for a regular Board of Education meeting held December 13, 2022 at 7:00 p.m. local time. The circulated copy has blanks for members present and absent, for the mover and supporter, and for the AYES and NAYS roll, and is certified by Gary Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education, with a recital of compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of 1976.

**Voter authorization**
At the General School Election held November 8, 2022, qualified electors approved bonds issuable in one or more series in an amount not to exceed $555,000,000 (the 2022 Bond Proposal) for remodeling, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and re-furnishing school buildings, athletic fields, playgrounds and other facilities; erecting and completing, equipping and furnishing a replacement middle school and classroom additions and other additions; acquiring and installing instructional technology infrastructure and equipment; acquiring, preparing, developing and improving sites; and the purchase of school buses.

**Bond parameters**

| Term | Provision |
|---|---|
| First series maximum | not to exceed $190,000,000 |
| Denomination | $5,000 or integral multiples |
| Maturity dates | May 1 or November 1, as determined at sale |
| Final maturity | not later than 30 years from date of issue |
| Maximum true interest cost | 6.50% per annum |
| Interest payment dates | semi-annually, May 1 and November 1 |
| Underwriter's discount cap | 0.50% of principal amount |
| Record date | fifteenth day of the month prior to payment |

Bonds may be issued in book-entry-only form through The Depository Trust Company in New York, New York, as serial or term bonds, subject to optional or mandatory redemption as determined at sale.

**Funds and tax pledge**
The Treasurer is to open a 2023 School Building and Site Bonds Debt Retirement Fund unless a Common Debt Retirement Fund is used, and a 2023 School Building and Site Bonds Projects Fund for net proceeds and net original issue premium. Commencing with the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2023, the District must levy annually a tax sufficient to pay principal and interest, without limitation as to rate or amount under Article IX, Sections 6 and 16 of the Michigan Constitution of 1963.

**Professionals and process**
Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated is appointed senior managing underwriter; Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. is appointed bond counsel, with disclosure of its periodic unrelated representation of Stifel; PFM Financial Advisors LLC is appointed Municipal Advisor. The Superintendent and the Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, either acting individually, serve as Authorized Officer with power to negotiate and execute the bond purchase agreement, execute a sale order, seek ratings and bond insurance, and approve official statements. A negotiated sale was chosen over competitive sale for flexibility in structuring maturities and timing. Treasury qualification is pursued under Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001 and the School Bond Qualification, Approval, and Loan Act, Act 92, Public Acts of Michigan, 2005.

**Exhibits**
Exhibit A is the bond form naming Cede & Co. as registered owner, citing Act 451, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, interest on a 360-day year of twelve 30-day months, and redemption notice 30 to 60 days in advance. Exhibit B is the Continuing Disclosure Undertaking under SEC Rule 15c2-12, requiring annual filing through MSRB EMMA by the last day of the sixth month after fiscal year end, commencing with the fiscal year ending June 30, 2023. Exhibit C is the Application for Final Qualification of Bonds. Identifier 39939819.
2022_31_2_d_bond_resolution_sbqlp_troy_2.verbose:
**Caption and posture.** Captioned TROY SCHOOL DISTRICT, COUNTY OF OAKLAND, State of MICHIGAN, RESOLUTION AUTHORIZING 2023 School Building and Site Bonds (UNLIMITED TAX GENERAL OBLIGATION). It recites that it was offered at a regular meeting of the Board of Education of the Troy School District held in the School District on December 13, 2022, at 7:00 p.m., local time. The packet copy leaves the PRESENT and ABSENT member lists blank, leaves blank the members offering and supporting the resolution, and leaves the AYES and NAYS lines blank; Gary Hauff, Secretary, Board of Education, signs twice, once beneath "RESOLUTION DECLARED ADOPTED" and once certifying the document as a true and complete copy of a resolution adopted at a regular meeting held December 13, 2022, conducted with public notice given in full compliance with the Open Meetings Act, Act 267, Public Acts of 1976, as amended.

**Recitals.** At the General School Election held in the School District on November 8, 2022, qualified electors approved the issuance of bonds, in one or more series, in an amount not to exceed $555,000,000, the 2022 Bond Proposal. Approved purposes are remodeling, equipping, re-equipping, furnishing and re-furnishing school buildings, athletic fields, playgrounds and other facilities; erecting and completing, equipping and furnishing a replacement middle school and classroom additions and other additions to existing school buildings and other facilities; acquiring and installing instructional technology infrastructure and equipment; and acquiring sites, preparing, developing and improving sites at school buildings and other facilities and the purchase of school buses, collectively the Projects. Under Section 6, Article IX and Section 16, Article IX of the Michigan Constitution of 1963, tax levies for these bonds are without limitation as to rate or amount. The Board authorizes a first series not to exceed $190,000,000 to pay Project and issuance costs, and designates the Superintendent and the Assistant Superintendent, Business Services, either one acting individually, as the Authorized Officer empowered to accept an underwriter's offer, negotiate, approve and execute a bond purchase agreement, and approve other terms and documents. The School District must either be granted qualified status within the meaning of Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001, as amended, or receive prior approval from the Michigan Department of Treasury.

**Bond details.** The Bonds are designated 2023 School Building and Site Bonds (Unlimited Tax General Obligation), issuable in one or more series with name, designation or suffix changes as appropriate, in an aggregate principal amount not to exceed $190,000,000 or such lesser amount as the Authorized Officer determines upon sale. They are registered as to principal and interest in the denomination of $5,000 or integral multiples, dated as of the date of delivery or another date set by the Authorized Officer, and numbered as determined by the Transfer Agent. Bonds mature on May 1 or November 1 in years and amounts set at sale, with final maturity not later than thirty (30) years from the date of issue. Interest is set upon negotiated sale at a rate or rates not exceeding a true interest cost of six and one-half percent (6.50%) per annum, payable semi-annually on May 1 and November 1. The underwriter's discount shall not exceed 0.50% of the principal amount. Principal is payable at a bank or trust company selected by the Authorized Officer serving as registrar and transfer agent. Interest is paid by check drawn on the Transfer Agent and mailed to the registered owner of record as of the fifteenth day of the month prior to each payment date, a date the District may change to conform to market practice. Bonds may be issued in book-entry-only form through The Depository Trust Company in New York, New York, as serial or term bonds or both, subject to optional or mandatory redemption at times, in the manner and at prices determined by the Authorized Officer. Official notice of redemption must state at minimum the original issue date, maturity dates, interest rates, CUSIP numbers if any, certificate numbers and called amounts for partial redemptions, the redemption date, the redemption price, the surrender location, and that interest ceases to accrue after the redemption date.

**Execution and funds.** Bonds follow the form in Exhibit A, signed by manual or facsimile signatures of the President and Secretary of the Board, and are invalid until authenticated by the Transfer Agent, which delivers them to the purchaser on instructions from the Treasurer of the Board upon payment. Unless a Common Debt Retirement Fund is established, the Treasurer shall open a special depositary account designated the 2023 School Building and Site Bonds Debt Retirement Fund, into which all tax proceeds levied for principal, interest and redemption price, plus any accrued interest received on delivery, are deposited and used solely for those payments. The Treasurer shall also establish the 2023 School Building and Site Bonds Projects Fund, holding amounts specified by the Authorized Officer from net sale proceeds and any net original issue premium, used only for Project costs and issuance costs and, as necessary, to rebate arbitrage earnings to the United States Department of Treasury under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, as amended. Net original issue premium may be used for capitalized interest or to reduce the principal amount issued and shall be counted against the 2022 Bond Proposal. Remaining moneys after Project completion may be used first for any purpose permitted by the 2022 Bond Proposal, second for any purpose permitted by law, and then transferred to the Debt Retirement Fund.

**Unlimited tax pledge.** Commencing with the fiscal year beginning July 1, 2023, the School District has a duty to levy annually a tax sufficient so that estimated collections will promptly pay principal and interest when due, without limitation as to rate or amount.

**Sale method and professionals.** Having considered competitive and negotiated sale, and on the advice of the Municipal Advisor, the District determined a negotiated sale provides greater flexibility in structuring maturities and timing and will enable better marketing to the advantage of the School District and its taxpayers. Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated is appointed senior managing underwriter; the Authorized Officer may appoint co-managing underwriters if recommended by the Municipal Advisor, may award the sale within the resolution's parameters, and may execute the bond purchase agreement and a sale order without further Board approval. Miller, Canfield, Paddock and Stone, P.L.C. is appointed bond counsel, with the Board approving that representation notwithstanding Miller Canfield's periodic representation in unrelated matters of Stifel, Nicolaus & Company, Incorporated and other potential parties. PFM Financial Advisors LLC is appointed financial advisor, the Municipal Advisor. The Authorized Officer may apply for bond ratings and purchase municipal bond insurance if deemed appropriate by the Municipal Advisor and Bond Counsel. The President of the Board and the Authorized Officer may each approve preliminary and final official statements and execute and deliver the final Official Statement and any amendments, ensuring the statements contain no untrue statement of material fact and omit no material fact necessary to make them not misleading.

**Disclosure, tax and Treasury.** The District covenants under SEC Rule 15c2-12 to provide the Exhibit B information, and covenants to take all actions within its control to maintain the exclusion of interest on the Bonds from adjusted gross income for federal income tax purposes under the Internal Revenue Code of 1986, including arbitrage rebate and the expenditure and investment of bond proceeds. The Authorized Officer may apply to Treasury for prior approval or file a qualifying statement, request waivers including rating waivers, and file a Security Report pursuant to the Act. District officers may seek interim approval and qualification under the School Bond Qualification, Approval, and Loan Act, Act 92, Public Acts of Michigan, 2005, as amended; the Authorized Officer may approve the Application for Final Qualification substantially in the form of Exhibit C and sign loan agreements, and the Secretary of the Board is directed to execute and submit the completed Application to Treasury. Officers, administrators, agents and attorneys may pay costs of issuance including Bond Counsel fees, Municipal Advisor fees, rating agency fees, Transfer Agent fees, and costs of printing the preliminary and official statements. All conflicting resolutions are rescinded.

**Exhibit A, Bond Form.** Names Cede & Co. as Registered Owner, with blanks for Interest Rate, Maturity Date of May 1, 20__, Date of Original Issue, and CUSIP. Interest is computed on a 360-day year consisting of twelve 30-day months. The bond recites issuance under Act 451, Public Acts of Michigan, 1976, as amended, and Act 34, Public Acts of Michigan, 2001, as amended, pursuant to the resolution adopted December 13, 2022, as the first series authorized by majority vote of electors at the General School Election held November 8, 2022. The full faith and credit of the School District is irrevocably pledged and the District must levy annually sufficient taxes without limitation as to rate or amount. Redemption notice is mailed at least 30 days and not more than 60 days prior to the redemption date; bonds are called in multiples of $5,000, with no further interest accruing after the redemption date if funds are on hand. The Transfer Agent need not register a transfer during the 15 days before mailing a redemption notice. Signature blocks provide for the President and countersigning Secretary and a Transfer Agent Certificate of Authentication dated in 2023.

**Exhibit B, Continuing Disclosure Undertaking.** Defines Audited Financial Statements prepared as required by Act 2, Public Acts of Michigan, 1968, as amended, along with Bondholders, EMMA (the MSRB's Electronic Municipal Market Access system), Financial Obligation, MSRB, Rule, and SEC. The District must file through EMMA on or before the last day of the sixth month after its fiscal year end, commencing with the fiscal year ending June 30, 2023, annual financial information and operating data matching Official Statement tables on Enrollment - Historical Enrollment; State Aid Payments; Property Valuations - History of Valuations; Major Taxpayers; School District Tax Rates (per $1,000 of Valuation); Tax Levies and Collections; Retirement Plan - Contribution to MPSERS; Debt Statement - Direct Debt; School Loan Revolving Fund (SLRF) Program; and General Fund Budget Summary in Appendix C, together with the Audited Financial Statements, with unaudited statements filed if the audit is not ready. Failure to disclose must be noticed timely. Sixteen enumerated events require notice within ten business days, including payment delinquencies, material non-payment defaults, unscheduled draws on debt service reserves or credit enhancements, adverse tax opinions and IRS determinations including Notices of Proposed Issue (IRS Form 5701-TEB), material bond calls and tender offers, defeasances, rating changes, bankruptcy or receivership, material mergers or asset sales, and material incurrence of or default under a Financial Obligation. Materiality is determined under federal securities laws; the obligation terminates when the District is no longer an obligated person, including upon legal defeasance; enforcement is limited to specific performance and non-compliance is not an event of default on the Bonds.

**Exhibit C.** Form of Application for Final Qualification of Bonds. The document carries the internal identifier 39939819.
